ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [m]_q = (1−q^m)/(1−q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k−1} (1−aq^j), let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k, and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Prove that for positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r ≤ d, and for every integer n > 1 with n ≡ 1 mod 2d, we have Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^(k(d−dk−2r)/2) / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k ≡ [rn]_q q^(r(1−n)/2) mod [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.

domain_restrictions: q is treated as a formal indeterminate.
m is an integer parameter in the q-integer definition.
a, b, and c are formal parameters in the q-shifted factorial notation.
j is an integer index running from 0 to k minus 1 in the product defining the q-shifted factorial.
k is a nonnegative integer in the notation definitions and a summation index from 0 to n minus 1 in the theorem.
d and r are positive integers.
gcd(d, r) = 1.
r is less than or equal to d.
n is an integer greater than 1.
n is congruent to 1 modulo 2d.
The modulus is the product of the q-integer [n]_q and the square of the nth cyclotomic polynomial Phi_n(q).
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every positive integers d and r with gcd(d, r) = 1 and r less than or equal to d, and every integer n greater than 1 with n congruent to 1 modulo 2d, the finite sum from k = 0 to n minus 1 of the term [3 d k plus r]_q times (q^r, q^r, q^d; q^(2d))_k times (q^d; q^d)_k squared times q to the power k(d minus d k minus 2r) divided by 2, all divided by (q^(2d); q^(2d))_k, is congruent modulo [n]_q times Phi_n(q)^2 to [r n]_q times q to the power r(1 minus n) divided by 2.
quantifier_order: For the notation, define the q-integer and q-shifted factorials for arbitrary formal parameters q, m, a, b, c, with k a nonnegative integer and j ranging from 0 to k minus 1.
For all positive integers d and r such that gcd(d, r) = 1 and r is less than or equal to d.
For every integer n greater than 1 such that n is congruent to 1 modulo 2d.
For the finite sum over k from 0 to n minus 1, the congruence statement holds.

payload.statement_nl: Let [m]_q=(1-q^m)/(1-q). For any parameter u and integer k>=0, let (u;q)_k:=∏_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-u q^j), and let (u,v,w;q)_k:=(u;q)_k(v;q)_k(w;q)_k. Let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial, and define M_n(q):=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. Suppose d and r are positive integers with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d, and suppose n>1 satisfies n ≡ 1 mod 2d. Define U_{d,n}(q):=∏_{j=1}^{n-1}(1+q^{dj}), define T_{d,r,n}(q):=∑_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k, define R_{d,r,n}(q):=[rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2}, and define G_{d,r,n}(q):=U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)). Then G_{d,r,n}(q) is divisible by M_n(q) in the Laurent polynomial ring Q[q,q^{-1}]. Equivalently, there exists H_{d,r,n}(q) in Q[q,q^{-1}] such that U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q))=M_n(q)H_{d,r,n}(q) in Q(q).

result_payload.candidate_counterexample: d=1, r=1, n=3 with ζ a primitive cube root of unity. Then U_{1,3}(ζ)=(1+ζ)(1+ζ^2)=1, R_{1,1,3}(ζ)=[3]_ζ·ζ^{-1}=0, and T_{1,1,3}(ζ)=1-9ζ^2≠0 (k=0 contributes 1, k=1 contributes -9ζ^2, k=2 vanishes because of the factor 1-q^3). Hence G_{1,1,3}(ζ)=1-9ζ^2≠0, but M_3(ζ)=[3]_ζΦ_3(ζ)^2=0.

result_payload.reason: The submitted proof is empty, and the lemma itself is refuted by the provided admissible instance d=1, r=1, n=3. Let ζ be a primitive cube root of unity. Then U_{1,3}(ζ)=(1+ζ)(1+ζ^2)=1. Also R_{1,1,3}(ζ)=[3]_ζ·ζ^{-1}=0 because [3]_ζ=1+ζ+ζ^2=0. For T_{1,1,3}, the k=0 term is 1, the k=1 term is -(1-ζ)^4=-9ζ^2, and the k=2 term is 0 because (q;q^2)_2 contains 1-q^3. Hence T_{1,1,3}(ζ)=1-9ζ^2≠0, so G_{1,1,3}(ζ)=U_{1,3}(ζ)(T_{1,1,3}(ζ)-R_{1,1,3}(ζ))=1-9ζ^2≠0. But M_3(ζ)=[3]_ζ·Φ_3(ζ)^2=0. If G_{1,1,3}(q)=M_3(q)H(q) with H in Q[q,q^{-1}], then evaluating at ζ (allowed since ζ≠0) would force G_{1,1,3}(ζ)=0, contradiction. Therefore the divisibility statement is false.
